name: VNC (Virtual Network Computing) from the Internet
description: Detects network traffic from an external system to an internal system on VNC-related ports 5800 through 5810. This shows a connection or connection attempt; it does not prove that a VNC session was established or that remote control occurred.
note:
Investigation

1. Check the external source, internal destination, exact port, time, firewall action, and whether the traffic was allowed.
2. Confirm whether the source is an approved VPN, supplier, or remote-support address and whether the destination should provide VNC.
3. Check the destination for successful authentication, VNC session records, endpoint evidence, and related threat alerts.
4. Review repeated attempts and any accompanying scanning or exploitation activity.

Response

Do not automatically block or isolate the system from this alert alone. Confirm ownership and authorisation. Escalate unexplained or unauthorised VNC activity, or a confirmed successful session, through the approved incident-response process.
author: Elastic
false_positives: VNC connections may be received directly to Linux cloud server instances but such connections are usually made only by engineers. VNC is less common than SSH or RDP but may be required by some work-flows such as remote access and support for specialized software products or servers. Such work-flows are usually known and not unexpected. Usage that is unfamiliar to server or network owners can be unexpected and suspicious.
